name: Button
summary: Trigger for an action or navigation. The primary interactive control.

a11y.keyboardNote: Measured in a browser on 2026-08-27 (apps/keyboard-probe + tests/visual/teclado-motor.spec.ts). Confirmed: Enter, Space.

props.name: variant
props.type: primary | secondary | outline | ghost | primary-outline | primary-ghost | danger | danger-outline | danger-ghost | link | link-primary | link-danger | nav
props.description: A shortcut for the (appearance, tone) pair; the two-axis API is appearance + tone. `secondary` is the neutral fill with the brand-coloured label; `tertiary` the neutral fill with the plain label (the default).

props.name: appearance
props.description: How much weight the box carries. nav is an appearance of its own (a navigation item), not a tone.

props.name: tone
props.type: neutral | brand | danger | success | warning | info
props.description: What the colour means. Every tone works with every appearance, filled included — each has its own colour and text pair per theme.

props.name: size
props.description: Height comes from the density tokens; the pill radius never changes.

props.name: href
props.description: Renders an <a> with the same skin. A button that navigates is a link.

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows the spinner, sets aria-busy and blocks interaction. The label stays.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Native disabled: the control leaves the tab order entirely. With href it becomes aria-disabled, since a link has no disabled state. USE IT WHEN THERE IS NOTHING TO EXPLAIN — measured on 2026-08-13, a disabled button cannot be focused, so a Tooltip hung on it is never read by anyone navigating with a keyboard, and wrapping it in a span (what other libraries document) fixes the pointer and not the keyboard, because the span comes in at tabIndex -1.

props.name: aria-disabled
props.description: Inert but REACHABLE: the control keeps its place in the tab order and announces itself as disabled, and this component blocks activation — the attribute is semantics only, so leaving it to the browser would announce "disabled" on a button that still acts. Use it when there IS a why to tell, and put the why in a Tooltip, which now reaches. There is no permission component in Aurea and there will not be one: hiding an action is {can ? … : …} in your own code, and hiding a button is not security — see ADR-0023.

props.name: leadingIcon
props.description: Glyph before the label.

props.name: trailingIcon
props.description: Glyph after the label.

props.name: type
props.description: Deliberately not submit: a Cancel inside a form must not fire the main action.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Stretches to the container. Only the width changes — the pill radius is invariant.

props.name: pressed
props.description: DEPRECATED, removed in 1.0 — use <Toggle>. It only paints and announces (aria-pressed) and YOU keep the state; Toggle owns the state, returns onPressedChange and demands an accessible name when it is icon-only. On, it shows the raised capsule with a yellow underline.

props.name: kbd
props.description: Shortcut shown as a Kbd inside the button and announced with aria-keyshortcuts.

props.name: grow
props.description: In a row (Cluster), takes an equal share with the other buttons that also grow. `fullWidth` asks for the whole line instead.

props.name: target
props.description: Link attribute, only with `href`.

props.name: rel
props.description: Link attribute, only with `href`.

props.name: download
props.description: Link attribute, only with `href`.

props.name: render
props.description: The element drawn instead of the <button>/<a> — your router's link, e.g. render={<Link href="/reports" />}. It receives the button's skin, content (icons, label, shortcut) and attributes; the destination is its own. Disabled or loading, its click is blocked too, like the disabled link.

props.name: share
props.type: { url?: string; title?: string; text?: string }
props.description: The button shares. It asks the browser whether it can share this link (navigator.canShare) — detecting the capability, not guessing the device. If it can (phones; Chrome, Edge and Safari on desktop), the device's share sheet opens, and cancelling is not an error. If it cannot, it copies the link and shows "Link copied" anchored to the button, at the button's size. If the copy fails, it says so and shows the link selected. The notice speaks to the screen reader. Without url, it is the page's address. Needs the AureaProvider (or aurea.js on the page) to give the notice; it emits [data-aurea-share], which aurea.js also reads. Only on a <button> (ignored with href or render). On native, the same name opens the system share sheet.
